items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: And as far as the overall expression that happens, that’s up to Edgar. ... I will be with them

ctx.x: Great. Was some of this music not notated — how do I put it — there was some room for interpretation.

Yes. When you think about for instance the opening section of “Sunrise” for cello and piano is written in noteheads. There were no stems and no bar lines, no expression marks, nothing, merely the noteheads. And it might be a filled-in notehead to a notehead that wouldn’t be filled in, which would indicate perhaps a longer, that I desired for that note to be held longer. But as far as the overall expression that happens, that’s up to Edgar. And I will do some more pieces like that for Joan because what it does is…
The music, a lot of it seems to lend itself to some visual images. Has anybody ever approached you about doing that?
